name: rura
desc: Interactive TUI scratchpad for building shell pipelines
why: An interactive scratchpad for building pipelines live is a fresh way to watch shell data flow step by step.

brief.what_it_is: Rura is a terminal UI (TUI) for building shell pipelines. You type a pipeline such as grep | sort | uniq into an input line, and its output appears in a pane that updates as you edit. You can run the pipeline in full or only up to a chosen subcommand, inspect any stage's output, diff outputs between runs, and save commands as presets. Input can come from a file passed with --file, from piped stdin, or from an initial command passed with --command.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says Rura replaces the usual loop of editing a pipe, pressing up-arrow, and rerunning it. It presents itself as a way to see shell data flow stage by stage while you build a pipeline.
brief.how_it_works: Commands run through a configurable shell (sh by default on Unix, powershell on Windows), and the README says Rura caches the output of subcommands to speed up iteration. Live modes re-execute the pipeline as you type, with a debounce delay (default 500 ms), and the Alt+\ binding runs the pipeline only up to the cursor's subcommand. Tab completion uses the system's bash, zsh, or fish tools.

brief.install_notes: Pre-built binaries are on the GitHub Releases page; packages exist for Homebrew, AUR, Debian/Ubuntu (.deb), Fedora/RHEL (.rpm), NixOS, and crates.io. No account or hardware is mentioned. Optional configuration is a TOML file at ~/.config/rura/config.toml on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/rura/config.toml on macOS, or %APPDATA%\rura\config.toml on Windows; the path can be overridden with --config or the RURA_CONFIG environment variable. The shell is chosen from --shell, then the config's shell key, then the SHELL environment variable, then sh. rura --default-config prints the default config. Presets, history, and logs are stored in per-user directories under the same app name.
brief.standout: Live partial-pipeline execution is the main hook: the Alt+\ binding runs the pipe only up to the cursor, and a diff base can be set to any subcommand's output, so you can compare what one stage produced across edits. Output caching and a 'Live Until Cursor' mode are less common in shell-pipeline tools.
brief.status: unknown. The README shows no release date, version number, changelog, or last-commit date, and the fetched page did not include repository activity. The Releases page and Repology badge were linked but not fetched.
brief.caveats: Clipboard copy (Ctrl+q) on Linux may lose its content on exit unless a clipboard manager is running, according to the README. Tab completion needs bash, zsh, or fish installed. Vim mode is optional. Default shell is sh on Unix and powershell on Windows, so behaviour can differ from a user's login shell unless configured. The NixOS install snippet in the README is labelled with a stray code-fence language tag ('aiignore'), which is cosmetic. Source build via cargo is an option but no build-time dependencies are described. Licensed under MIT.
